title: Review of c06's pcell yeff-response finding: replicates on fresh seed 7 (mean yield 1.06 vs marker 0.99 at t=25500, then a crash to one giant cell by t~40000)
summary: Ran the finding's world.py on seed 7 with genealogy.py to t=60000 (11 persistent splits, gen 2, 0 merges, 31 deaths) and with labkit (to t=6000 only: 120 frames at this world's 50 steps per frame; cells form from the uniform particle soup by t~800). Mean yield vs inert marker over time: 1.00/1.00 (t=5500), 1.02/1.02 (15500), 1.04/1.01 (20500), 1.06/0.99 (25500, 18 cells), 1.14/1.02 (30500, 8 cells), 1.22/0.98 (35500, 5 cells), then 1 cell from t~40000 to the end (1.37/1.00 at t=60000). Dying mature cells keep their absolute yield (1.022 at birth, 1.041 at death; 37% declined) while the population moves past them (1.024 -> 1.124). So the response against the marker and the runaway to giant cells both replicate; here the crash comes earlier (t~30000-40000) than on the finding's seeds.

observations.H: summary_s7.txt: mean yield 1.06 vs marker 0.99 at t=25500 and 1.14 vs 1.02 at t=30500; dying cells' absolute yield 1.022 -> 1.041; population 18 -> 1 cell by t~40000

seeds_run.result: response vs marker replicates; crash to one giant cell by t~40000

controls_run.H: inert marker zm in the same seed-7 genealogy

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The response is measured on a shrinking population: by the time yield has risen ~0.1 above the marker the population is already collapsing (8 cells), so the clean window is t~20000-30000 only. The labkit pack covers only t<=6000.
